MeitY's advisory to Meta directs the suppression of protest reporting on Instagram and Facebook. It must be withdrawn.

19 Oct 2026

On 10 October 2026, the Cyber Laws Division of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology issued an advisory to Meta Platforms bearing File No. 6(2)/2026-Cyberlaws. It was not published on the MEITY website and first HT and then PTI reported it on 18 October. Any such advisory is not a legal order and MEITY is not legally empowered to issue them on the basis of any statutory provision. This advisory followed, by two days, an advisory of 8 October to all social media intermediaries calling for "enhanced diligence" over content on "ongoing public events", asking platforms to "label or add context" to misleading content and to "give priority to complaints from authorised Government agencies".  IFF called for the withdrawal of that advisory on 9 October. The Meta advisory was issued on the day the Delhi Police detained protesters and journalists at the demonstrations called over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

The advisory states that content relating to "public-order and law and order situations" is being "prominently displayed and recommended" on Meta's platforms and, "when presented without adequate context or disproportionately amplified", "may contribute to public confusion, apprehension and disturbance of public order and social tranquillity". It singles out "unverified or misleading claims regarding the imposition of emergency, restrictions, police action or other official measures". Further, Meta is advised to review its "recommendation and content ranking mechanisms", to ensure its systems "do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives", and to furnish "information or assistance" to law enforcement, "with immediate effect". PTI reports that the Ministry acted on inputs from "agencies" that Meta's platforms were not promoting all "narratives" equally.

This advisory matches restrictions on META platforms related to protest content and reporting in the same timline. On 10 October, the Instagram account of Molitics India was withheld in India. On 11 October, a Mathrubhumi English reel showing a woman clinging to a pole as police officers attempted to detain her was restricted citing, "a notice from the Government of India/Law Enforcement", and a video report by Observer Post Hindi was restricted on Facebook by what Meta called an "automated system" acting under the IT Rules, 2021. On 12 October, the Instagram account of journalist Shubhangi Das Gupta was restricted in India for alleged non-compliance with "local IT Rules". On 13 October, the account of Journo Mirror (about five lakh followers) was withheld. The account of Fridays For Future India has since been withheld without any stated reason. Meta's notices to these users do not disclose what is unlawful about the content. 

As per notices shared by us by those who have been censored by META, they take two forms: 

1. "a notice from the Government of India/Law Enforcement under Section 79(3)(b)", and, 

2. "through an automated system implemented pursuant to legal requirements under India's Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules". 

Neither names the issuing agency, the order, the provision of law or offence the content is said to disclose, or the URL complained of. We know due to litigation that the first notice related to a Sahyog order issued by a Law Enforcement Agency (LEA), while the second one is without any legal order. At the same time, several users received no communication at all. Instagram used the same "automated system" notice against Anjali Priya, Varnika Dhawan and Sachin Gupta after the July protests, and against cartoonist Satish Acharya, who lost nine cartoons and then his account between February and September 2026. 

In April 2026, The Hindu reported that Meta automatically restricts government and police flagged content in India at scale, and seeks a separate government direction before restoring content later found to be legally unsupported. IFF objected to Meta on 4 May 2026. IFF condemns the advisory of 10 October and the restrictions imposed in its wake. An executive communication that instructs a platform to suppress "unverified" claims about "police action" and to correct a "limited set of narratives", issued on the day of a police crackdown and kept from the public, is a censorship directive in all but name.  It makes the State the editor of what Indians may see of a protest against the State. IFF calls upon MeitY to withdraw it and upon Meta to disclose what it has done under it.

Our demands

1. MeitY must withdraw the advisories of 8 and 10 October 2026 forthwith and publish them.

2. MeitY must abandon proposed Rule 3(4) and restrict content only by reasoned, published orders under Section 69A or notices compliant with Rule 3(1)(d).

3. Meta must disclose every takedown, account restriction and act of downranking carried out under the advisories, and its compliance report to the Ministry.

4. Meta must restore the accounts and posts of journalists, outlets and creators restricted since 8 October 2026 unless it holds a valid legal order, and must furnish that order to the person affected.

5. Meta must suspend the automated restriction of content in India and disclose on what inputs its "automated system" acts.

Any person whose account or content has been withheld in India since 8 October 2026 may write to IFF at legal@internetfreedom.in. IFF is providing assistance pro bono.

“Democracy is not merely about elections. It is about equal rights, independent institutions, freedom of expression and protection for every citizen.”

In this speech, Vijaylakshmi Nadar, identified in the video as a New Jersey member of the International Federation of Journalists, USA, raises serious concerns about the Modi government's political ideology, the RSS, Hindutva politics and their alleged impact on India's democratic institutions and religious minorities.

Her central message is that the international community and the Indian diaspora should not ignore questions of democratic accountability, minority rights and freedom of expression.

These concerns deserve serious, evidence-based public examination. Human Rights Watch's World Report 2026 documents concerns about the treatment of religious minorities, pressure on government critics and restrictions on freedom of expression in India. Reuters has also reported on rising anti-minority hate-speech incidents documented by India Hate Lab. These are independently reportable human-rights concerns, not proof that every allegation made in the speech is established.

THE QUESTIONS DEMOCRACY CANNOT IGNORE

• Are India's democratic institutions sufficiently independent and accountable?

• Are religious minorities, including Muslims, Christians and Sikhs, and historically marginalised communities receiving equal protection under the law?

• Can journalists, activists and government critics speak freely without intimidation or disproportionate legal action?

• Should allegations of political interference, discrimination or abuse be examined by genuinely independent institutions?

Criticism of a government is not hatred of a country. Defending India's constitutional democracy means demanding equal citizenship, justice, accountability and dignity for all Indians, regardless of religion or political belief.

Every serious allegation deserves impartial scrutiny. Where wrongdoing is established, accountability must follow; where allegations are disproved, that finding must also be respected.

France: pre-insurrectional conflagration (surprised?)
----

1 France

The thugs, looters, black blocs, vandals and idiots who parasitized the processions of protesters, high-school students, trade unionists, ordinary impoverished people and left-wing bourgeois on Saturday in France put on an exceptional “performance” that has left the country stunned and the foreign press appalled. The scenes of insurrection, sometimes to the cry of “Revolution,” appeared more intense than the 2023 riots known as the Nahel riots (even though at the time 95 departments and hundreds of communes were affected, around 50,000 rioters, 12,000 vehicles burned, 2,500 buildings damaged or burned, thousands of arrests and detentions) and also than the action days of the Yellow Vests in 2018-2019.

In the streets of Paris as well as in those of the country’s main cities, hundreds of institutions and businesses were targeted, leaving entire streets littered with debris and the carcasses of burned two-wheelers in city centers. In Marseille, Lille, Angers and Bordeaux, protesters broke into town halls or prefectures to vandalize them. In Lyon, a tourist office branch was set on fire. In Limoges, the 19th-century Town Hall was “largely lost” to the https://t.co/VlxEwBkLZR the capital, “entire streets were methodically ravaged,” according to Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire (PS). Together with his counterparts from Lyon and Marseille, he asked to be received early next week by Prime Minister Sébastien https://t.co/YiYVFRHjIT total, 1,200 people were arrested on Saturday and 150 police officers and gendarmes were injured, according to the executive. Several protesters were also injured, some seriously, notably in Saint-Étienne, where a 17-year-old had his hand torn off by a police grenade.

----

2 Ukraine

Marco Rubio tried on Saturday evening to downplay Donald Trump’s decision to exempt Russia from new sanctions, insisting it was a 60-day pause aimed “sort of at ‘analyzing’ their economic repercussions.” Marco, Canard Hirsute likes you since you’re the only adult in the White House, but this is what’s called backpedaling in the semolina. A few hours earlier, Republican figures, in addition to Democrats, had attacked Donald Trump’s decision not to apply the so-called “Graham” law, named after a senator close to him who unfortunately died this summer. “It’s completely irresponsible,” denounced Republican Senator Thom Tillis, a frequent critic of the American president on diplomatic issues. This exemption is a “mistake,” judged Ted Cruz, another influential Republican senator. 

“Trump has just given Putin his best birthday present,” underlined the leading Democratic voice in the Senate, Chuck Schumer. Donald Trump’s decision to exempt Russia from major new sanctions is an “encouragement” for Vladimir Putin, Volodymyr Zelensky denounced on Saturday, while Moscow for its part welcomed a “historic moment.”The Ukrainian president stated that the decision came on the very day Russia struck 15 important electrical infrastructures across Ukraine, in one of the “largest” attacks against the country’s energy network.

------

3 Israel

Masked Jewish settlers attacked Palestinians, representatives of the Catholic Church and European officials — the Belgian consul general, French and Polish diplomats as well as a French mayor — in the occupied West Bank, in a village mainly populated by Christian Palestinians (yes, that exists). 

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar condemned the attack, which he attributed to “Israeli rioters.” The attack came the day after settlers assaulted American photojournalist Heidi Levine, who was covering the olive harvest for the Washington Post.

--------------
4 India

Nobody in Europe gives a damn because it’s far away, but the protests in India concern respect for the rule of law and democracy in the most populous country on the planet. The leader of the “cockroaches” party, a youth movement born in the spring, was released on Saturday. 

The day after his arrest ahead of a demonstration in New Delhi against the revision of electoral rolls — which his movement considers favorable to the ultra-nationalist Hindu Prime Minister Narendra Modi — the founder of the Cockroach People’s Party (CJP), Abhijeet Dipke, 31, walked out of a police station on Saturday afternoon. Two other CJP leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, remain in detention.The electoral reform, launched last year to remove duplicates, the deceased and fraudsters from the electoral lists, has, according to counts published in the media and by the opposition, struck off 130 million registered voters.

---------

5 Albania

Clashes continued on Saturday for the fifth day in Tirana, where protesters are demanding the resignation of the head of the Albanian socialist government and denouncing teaching conditions and university tuition rights. Protesters threw stones at the police and set fire to trash bins. In the evening, fires were started in several buildings, including the Supreme Court and the entrance of the Bank of Albania. 

The Ministry of Health indicated that 35 people were injured on Saturday, including 18 members of the security forces and 17 protesters.For the first time since these gatherings began, the police used rubber bullets. Prime Minister Edi Rama denounced the presence of “foreign hands” behind this wave of protest.

---

Riyadh on Sunday acknowledged for the first time the combat death against the Houthis (Iran’s allies) of two soldiers, pilots of a helicopter shot down in Yemen.Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi declared for his part that his country stood ready to defend the kingdom if it “requested it,” specifying that any Egyptian deployment would require Parliament’s approval. Blocking TIP’s X accounts is a new form of banning a political party: Irfan Degirmenci

n an interview with The Amargi, Irfan Degirmenci, a member of the Workers’ Party of Turkey (TIP) Party Assembly, discussed access restrictions targeting the party’s X accounts, the legal decision concerning his own account, and the broader crackdown on political opposition, and LGBTQ+ communities in Turkey.

He calls for solidarity among groups facing censorship and says political struggle must continue beyond social media platforms.

The Amargi: TIP recently announced that access restriction decisions had been issued against the party’s headquarters and Istanbul provincial organization accounts on X. The party stated that it believes the decisions are connected to its statements and broadcasts exposing alleged corruption involving a fund. Why do you think this is happening now?

Irfan Degirmenci: I am not sure whether the account of any political party in Turkey has been blocked in this way before. It is almost like the closure of a political party.

Twenty years ago, they would physically seal the entrance to a party’s headquarters and remove people from the building in handcuffs. In the digital age, there is no need to do that anymore. If you can obtain a court order without respecting universal legal principles, you can act without even notifying the person or institution concerned.

They saw how effectively TIP could organize through social media and how seriously the party was pursuing one of the biggest corruption scandals in the country’s recent history. Initially, the government seemed uncertain about how to respond. Then it quickly took action.

The public was led to believe that those who had made billions through the fund would be held accountable. That expectation lasted two or three days before those who should have been held responsible began to escape accountability. Meanwhile, journalists reporting on the allegations have faced pressure, and some have been detained.

I believe TIP has become a target partly because it has pursued these allegations effectively. I also believe the publication, on our X account, of a video alleging Justice Minister Akin Gurlek’s responsibility in these developments played a role in the decision against our party’s accounts.

The Amargi: What will TIP do if the access restriction decisions are implemented?

Irfan Degirmenci: We have no intention of behaving as though everything is normal. If we simply said we rejected the decision and would pursue a legal challenge, we would be practicing the conventional opposition politics that already exists in Turkey.

We intend to make them regret closing our accounts. We will continue to be present in the streets and public squares. We have a strong culture of protest, and wherever those responsible go, we will continue asking what happened to the money taken from the funds.

We always have a Plan B and a Plan C. We have many methods of struggle, including those used in the 1970s [printing leaflets, selling street newspapers, and using traditional methods of political organizing]. This is also a struggle that extends beyond Turkey: as peoples, we must consider what we can do against the alliance between international capital and autocratic leaders.

We also have a digital strategy. People can follow the party’s activities, find out where protests are taking place, and stay informed about current developments on our TIP mobile application. We will continue creating alternative ways to communicate and organize.

The Amargi: Your own X account has also been subject to an access restriction decision. What is the current situation?

Irfan Degirmenci: I have not received any decision by email from X or directly from a court. I learned about it through news reports. A journalist colleague sent me a copy of the court decision and asked whether I knew about it. I did not.

The decision concerns approximately 200 accounts, issued by a court in Bakirkoy, Istanbul. According to the information I received, four journalists have been treated differently within that group: the decision indicates that even if we change our usernames, we will still be unable to access the platform through our existing user IDs.

They want to erase me from public life. It feels as though they are saying, “We can do this to you whenever we want.” They want to keep us away from social platforms and silence us.

The restriction has not yet been implemented against my account. I have not received direct notification, and I am still astonished by the situation.

The Amargi: If your account is eventually blocked, will you move to another platform, such as Bluesky?

Irfan Degirmenci: Our fundamental contradiction is that we continue to communicate through X, a platform owned by Elon Musk, while criticizing the support wealthy business figures provide to autocratic governments.

Unfortunately, X remains the most widely used platform, which makes it difficult to leave. A boycott could be effective, and we will try to organize one in Turkey. We need a new platform that people can collectively move to and recognize as their new address.

People keep calling for a move to Bluesky, yet they continue posting on X to maintain their reach. The peoples of the world have not yet succeeded in acting collectively in this regard.

Personally, I am 50 years old, but I still try to adapt to new technologies. Because they want to make me invisible, I am trying to become even more visible. I have resumed my YouTube broadcasts, am trying to increase my Instagram following, and plan to start broadcasting on TikTok soon. There is no shortage of ways to continue. The methods of struggle do not run out.

The Amargi: These restrictions are not limited to politicians and journalists. LGBTQ+ organizations and activists have also faced access restrictions, alongside pressure on human rights organizations. Do you see these developments as part of a broader intervention in social life?

Irfan Degirmenci: Absolutely. There seems to be no clear limit to how far this can go. Those organizing against this darkness must learn to act together, setting aside their differences.

An attempt is being made to impose a single model of life on society. A rigid and conservative understanding of morality is being imposed and used to maintain political power. Yet the ruling order itself has no genuine moral principles. If you want to judge morality, look not between people’s legs, but inside bank vaults.

We have heard arguments about protecting families from an alleged “international LGBTQ+ lobby.” But what they call the “LGBTQ+ lobby” consists of civil society organizations coming together to defend fundamental human rights, including organizations in Turkey.

We are talking about a government and intelligence apparatus capable of sending police to the doors of civil society organizations even when they hold closed meetings. During Pride months in June, we have had to share the routes of planned marches on paper rather than openly, because we do not know who might be listening.

The Amargi: Political opposition movements and LGBTQ+ communities already struggle to find adequate representation in mainstream media. How does restricting their social media accounts affect their ability to communicate and organize?

Irfan Degirmenci: These groups are often portrayed as enemies, even when they appear in mainstream media. Social media has therefore become an important space for them to communicate and make themselves visible. When these accounts are blocked, it becomes much harder for these people and organizations to reach the public.

We can see similar patterns elsewhere. In the United States, as the Trump administration has faced difficulties over foreign policy, including the war involving Iran, the government has increasingly targeted transgender Americans. Turkey is not entirely different in this respect. When the government finds itself in difficulty, it brings another issue to the forefront.

The Amargi: What kind of solidarity is necessary between political opposition movements, LGBTQ+ communities and other groups facing restrictions?

Irfan Degirmenci: We must recognize that these different forms of repression are connected. Those confronting them cannot afford to remain isolated from one another. The people who want to impose a single way of life on society benefit when different groups remain divided.

We must continue finding ways to organize, communicate and support one another, even when the methods available to us change. If one of us is facing difficulties, we must be there to support them.

Well, I don’t know about you, but I think 76-year-old Mr Miller deserves a bloody round of applause. 👏🇬🇧

Arrested for wearing a burqa at a protest, then turns up to court wearing the fucking burqa again….. Complete with handbag!🤣🤣

Sir, your level of sarcasm is absolutely outstanding. 🤣

Now, I’m no legal expert, but I do have a functioning brain cell, and even that’s struggling to comprehend the absolute shitshow we’ve become. We live in a country where we’re encouraged to embrace ourselves and individuality, freedom of expression and the right to identify however we please. I could identify as a fucking lampshade tomorrow, although knowing my luck, the government would find a way to tax me for electricity. 💡

Yet here’s a 76-year-old man claiming he’s exploring a religion, wearing religious clothing and asking for the same rules to apply to everyone. And suddenly he’s a criminal defendant?!

Mr Miller says he wasn’t even asked to remove his covering by police, and that his identity was captured on cameras. If that’s correct, surely his argument deserves to be heard!
And now the British taxpayer gets to fund the next instalment of this ridiculous circus.

Police time, court time, legal administration, another trial. Money money money! 💷 Meanwhile, pensioners are counting pennies and families are struggling.

Now, I understand there are laws about covering your face at certain protests. But I also understand the importance of challenging laws and how they’re applied. That’s rather the point of living in a democracy! Well I think that’s what is meant to be about?

Whether you agree with Mr Miller or not, you’ve got to admire a man who’s prepared to stand there, handbag in hand, and question the system. Because this isn’t really about a handbag or a burqa anymore. It’s about freedom and consistency and whether the same rules really do apply to everybody.

Personally, I’m Team Miller on this one. 🇬🇧

Anyway, I’m off to identify as a government-funded project. At least then somebody might throw some fucking money my way.

Mr Miller, take a bow. Preferably without dropping the handbag. 😂👏

“When I was pregnant with you I was under pressure to have an abortion but I refused. I chose instead to bring you into this world.” 

Excerpts from "Magoba Ga Uganda" the Auto Biography of Pastor Martin Ssempa..now Coming out later in Dec 2025. Give me some feedback. 

My mother did not hesitate to bring up the circumstances around my birth and conception every time I tried her patience as a young boy. Granted, she always told me she loved me, but I got to know my chequered history quite early. “Your father’s parents owned a shop and the women who worked there assured me that it was unacceptable and totally reprehensible, a taboo, for an African woman and an Asian man to get together, let alone produce a child from that union. The only solution they said, was to perform an abortion and end that life before it even began. But I refused!" 

I was conceived towards the end of the 60s, a few years into Uganda’s journey as an independent country, a few years before Idi Amin Dada started his rule in Uganda. I am told it was the time of miniskirts and twist dancing in Uganda, and the time of the American sex revolution! My father was a young Asian of (most likely) Indian descent whose family was one of the trading families in Masaka. 

He was a student at Makerere University, and that is the extent of my knowledge about my father. Soon after I was born, President Iddi Amin declared an economic war of indigenization and my father was among those who were deported/expelled out of Uganda. The History of Uganda is such that Asians, particularly Indians took the lion’s share of trading licences. President Amin wanted to reverse this unfair advantage but unfortunately, it meant I would never get to meet my father or his family. Not only was I born in a conflicted relationship of races, I never got a chance to know who my father was, nor his family. Despite the great love and acceptance that I received from my mother, siblings and my Baganda tribal family, I always felt a great sense of “father hunger” - that yearning for fatherly protection, provision and affirmation which only a Dad could provide. 

My mother was a primary school teacher who was struggling to raise eight children as a single parent. She had been married to James Kyeyune, a medical officer and they were blessed with six children but their marriage broke down. My mother always told me that she could not accept being a co-wife. My step father had brought another wife home and she could not accept the idea of sharing a husband. Despite the efforts of the good catholic bishops who intervened to smooth things over, the marriage broke down and she moved away in the mid-60s to start a new life as a teacher and a single mother. I was born into a family of seven other children, five boys and two girls. Dickson, the eldest had gone off to join the police force, Joseph the second born and Edward the fifth born stayed with their paternal grandparents. Clare and Fred were students in a Catholic boarding school and came home only during the holidays. This meant that the three youngest children Florence, John and myself were the ones who stayed home with mother. 

Owing to my bi-racial parentage, my looks were quite different from the rest of the family and the children around me. I had big curly hair unlike my brother’s kinky hair. I had much lighter skin due to my father’s suspected Asian descent. In our Baganda culture, the name of a child is based on the clan of the father and in the absence of my biological father, my mother gave me the names of her father, Ssempa which meant that I belonged to my mother’s clan; symbolically represented by the colobus monkey (Nkima). My grandfather, Alipo Ssempa was an educated British colonial government administrator and interpreter in Masaka. Sadly, I never got to meet him as death took him before we could meet. His father, Bisakka or Bishaka who was my great grandfather had been a noteworthy regional trader in the Buganda, Ankole, Bunyoro, Rwanda and Tanzania region. 

He was called Bisaka, a name very closely related to Kisaka which is a large cluster or collection of trees and bushes which occurs on the savannah plains and hills in this region. It’s like an individual collection of a family of trees and bushes which are separated from others by savannah grass fields. Just as his name implies, my great grandfather had eighty wives which made up his large family! Bisaka was known as Bishaka by the western Ankole-Rwanda tribes whose language is characterized by the ‘sh’ making him multi tribal/multi lingual and multi-wifey. Unfortunately, this great trader and lover of the sweet affections of the beautiful women of Buganda, Ankole, Rwanda and Tanzania region suffered an early death which led to the scattering of the whole family. 

My great grandmother "Venecka Munaku Atambuza Mwoyo" [the poor walks guided by the spirit] and her sister who had also been a co-wife branched out Eastward and settled between Mityebiri/ Minziro in Rakai and Buyikuzi in Lukaya which is half way between Kampala city and Masaka town. Thus I carried the genes of Bisaka and the name of his son Ssempa, a fact which made people do a double take every time they met the bi-racial child with a native African name. It was not the norm. 

These bio-genetical differences were much more pronounced in my childhood. I stuck out both in the classroom and on the children’s playfield. I can compare it to being the only black student in an all-white students school or being the only white student at an all-black-African students school. To some, I was an object of curiosity and I often had to bear the discomfort of having my hair felt, so the kids with kinky hair could feel my curly hair. Most of them were kind, but others would mock me with unkind words, ”Ssempa was forgotten at the airport, the Indians forgot him with the suitcases and boxes at the airport.” They would laugh and others gave me the monicker, ‘Magoba ga Uganda’ a Luganda phrase meaning “Ugandan profit” which they would explain with youthful logic; “In the interaction between Uganda and India, Ssempa was the Ugandan profit.” These were painful words casually thrown around by some misguided youngsters. They did not reflect the sentiment of the whole Buganda community which accepted me as a son. But in the places where children interacted with minimal adult supervision; the classrooms, playing fields where adults were absent to guide, I was often called painful names, like ‘illegitimate,’ ‘bastard,’ ‘magoba ga Uganda.’ It is a fact of life that some children will mock those who are different or handicapped, maybe they have unusually large ears or nose. This is the foolishness of childhood which fortunately disappears as we grow older. 

Narozali is found in Buyange Parish, Kyanamukakaaka subcounty in Masaka district in the South West of Uganda. It was a large Roman catholic parish with a church, schools and many other projects run by the church. It was located about one hour from Masaka town, on the undulating hills surrounding the shores of Lake Victoria. My mother was a grade one (primary one) teacher at the parish and we stayed in a house provided by the school. My mother was a devout catholic and we attended daily morning mass as well as family evening prayers. We prayed much when there was trouble such as when there was war in the period of 1971-72. In 1971, the president of Uganda, Apollo Milton Obote was overthrown by his star General, Idi Amin Dada in a military takeover that changed Uganda’s political and economic terrain in which I was to grow up. First, the expulsion of Asians in his economic war policy of indigenization was a strange mixture of tragedy and triumph. It was tragic to the Indians whose families had built and run the back bone of the Ugandan economy and were unceremoniously expelled from the country. Most of all the industries, commercial farms, large and small trading shops were owned and run by Indian families who had the technical skills, experience and passion to operate them effectively. They were forced to vacate all of this in a short time not knowing where they were to go. The sudden loss of homes and wealth which had been accumulated for nearly a century led some unfortunate souls to suicides by the river Nile. Others travelled to Canada, England, Kenya and United States where they started a new life. Some ended up succeeding incredibly in their new homes, becoming the economic entrepreneurs of their new homelands. Soon after Idi Amin became president of Uganda, there was an ill-fated attempt to attack and militarily overthrow him by rebels based out of Tanzania. 

Our home of Narozali is in the South West region of Uganda’s territory next to Tanzania and at times, it seemed that we were living in a war zone. Military vehicles, jeeps and noisy Israeli-made warplanes above made it difficult to ignore the ongoing conflict. We spent a lot of time praying to God to intervene and even added special supplications to the Virgin Mary who had a special altar with her monument encased in a specially made grotto. Here we earnestly recited the rosary and asked for divine intervention. Providentially, the war ended soon as the attackers were defeated in a bloody massacre! The early efforts by the coalition of anti-Idi Amini forces to remove him militarily were unsuccessful and suffered huge casualties. For the natives, it was also a mixture of triumph and tragedy. Their struggle for independence from colonial masters had given them political gains without economic gains. The economy was controlled by the Indian merchant families giving little or no space for the emergence of African owned enterprises. This all changed suddenly as Iddi Amin began to apportion out enterprises to the natives. My mother applied to operate a stone quarry but was denied for some reason. However, native Ugandan's got to own and operate all sorts of businesses from industries to merchant shops. While it is true that many ended up being mismanaged and run into the ground, there were others which succeeded. The expulsion of the Asians/ Indians created a leadership vacuum which forced many Ugandans to quickly learn to trade in various enterprises, giving rise to Ugandan owned business. 

As a child of dual Asian-Ugandan ancestry, it was a loss for my father’s people, and a gain for my mother’s people. As Nyinamwiru, the daughter of Bukuku lamented when she learnt that her father had been killed by her son Karabumbi Nduhura who was now the new king, “My ears cause me to hear both evil and good, for is it not my son who has killed Bukuku? My father is dead, but my son reigns, thus I have sorrow on one arm but joy on the other.” This historical account of our ancestors’ dilemma describes my conflicted view of Idi Amin’s expulsion of Indians from Uganda. This view was later to be articulated in my college days by a professor of Political Science at Makerere University who said that Amin’s expulsion of Indians was the single most significant event in economic empowerment of the Ugandan natives. It was quite interesting because, Professor Mahmood Mamdani, was a Ugandan with Asian ancestry, just like me. To date, Uganda, unlike its East African counterparts Kenya and Tanzania has the greatest number of Africans who own business while the other two have businesses still largely owned by the original Asian families who had no Iddi Amin to shake them up.

text:
In Constituent Assembly, Mr Tajamul Hussain argued that Muslims should not be given reservation but scheduled caste should be given. The excerpts are enclosed below 

Mr. President, Sir, reservation of seats in any shape or form and for any community or group of people is, in my opinion, absolutely wrong in principle. Therefore I am strongly of opinion that there should be no reservation of seats for anyone and I, as a Muslim, speak for the Muslims. There should be no reservation of seats for the Muslim community. (Hear, Hear). I would like to tell you that in no civilised country where there is parliamentary system on democratic lines, there is any reservation of seats. Take the case of England. The House of Commons is the mother of parliaments. There is no reservation of seats for community there. No doubt they had reservation of seats for the universities but even that has been abolished. What is reservation, Sir? Reservation is nothing but a concession, a safeguard a protection for the weak. We, Muslims do not want any concession. Do not want protection, do not want safeguards. We are not weak. This concession would do more harm than good to the Muslims. Reservation is forcing candidates on unwilling electorates. Whether the electorates wants us or not, we thrust ourselves on them. We do not want to thrust ourselves on unwilling electorates. The majority community will naturally think that we are encroaching upon their rights. We do not want them to think that. We must expert ourselves. Separate electorates have been a curse to India, have done incalculable harm to this country. It was invented by the British. Reservation is the offspring of separate electorates. Do not bring in reservation in the place of separate electorates. Separate electorates have barred our progress. Separate electorates have gone for ever. We desire neither reservation nor separate electorates. We want to merge in the nation. We desire to stand on our own legs. We do not want the support of anyone. We are not weak. We are strong. We are Indians first and we are all Indians and will remain Indians. We shall fight for the honour and glory of India and we shall die for it. (Applause). We shall stand united. There will be no divisions amongst Indians. United we stand; divided we fall. Therefore we do not want reservation. It means division. I ask the members of the majority community who are present here today:-Will you allow us to stand on our legs? Will you allow us to be a part and parcel of the nation? Will you us to be an  equal partner with you? Will you allow us to march shoulder to shoulder with you? Will you allow us to share your sorrows grief and joy? If you do, then for god’s sake keep your hands off reservation for the Muslim community. We do not want statutory safeguard. As I said before, we must stand on our own legs. If we do that, we will have no inferiority complex. We are not inferior to you in any way, Do not make us feel inferior by giving us this concession. I say emphatically there is no difference between you and me. Because we worship the same God by different names, in a different way, that is no reason why we should be considered a minority. We are not a minority. The term ‘minority’ is a British creation. The British created minorities. The British have gone and minorities have gone with them. Remove the term ‘minority’ from your dictionary. (Hear, Hear). There is no minority in India. Only so long as there were separate electorates and reservation of seats there was a majority community and a minority community.

I ask the majority community not to distrust the minorities now. The minorities have adjusted themselves. I will give you a concrete example. You remember the Hyderabad incident; you remember that before you took police action against Hyderabad, what happened. The majority community were afraid that there would be rioting of the Muslims if action was taken against Hyderabad. I was first man to speak about it about a year and half ago in the Central Legislature. I criticised the Government of India. I am sorry Sardar Patel was not present at that time when I was dealing with his portfolio, but my honourable Friend Mr. Gadgil was in charge. I criticised the action of the Government, I told them that they were absolutely mistaken in thinking that the Muslims would rise; they would adjust themselves. I said to them: “You march an army against Hyderabad and within couple of days, you would take the whole of Hyderabad.” I made a long speech and after my speech was over, there was a reply by the Honourable Minister in charge, Mr. Gadgil. He never spoke a single word about it and he never replied to my criticism, but I asked him: “You have replied to everybody’s criticism. Why not mine? I asked you to march an army against Hyderabad; you would take Hyderabad within a couple of days and there would be no rioting.” Mr. Gadgil “You are perfectly right and we will do it.”

I appeal to all minorities to join the majority in creating a secular State. In the new state of things, I want that every citizen in India should be able to rise to the fullest stature and that is why I say that reservation would be suicidal to the minority. I want the minorities to forget that they are minorities in politics. If they think they are minorities in politics, they will be isolated. If they are isolated, the feeling of frustration will cripple them. I do not want to remain minority. Do the minorities, I ask, expect to form part of the great nation and have a hand in the control of its destinies. Can they achieve that aspiration if they are isolated from the rest of India? The minorities if they are returned as minorities, i.e., by reservation of seats can never have an effective voice in the affairs of the country. They can never form a Government. Disraeli could never have formed a Government and could never have become the Prime Minister of England had there been reservation of seats for the Jews in England. I want the minorities to have an honourable place in the Union of India. National interests must always be placed over group interests. The minorities should look forward to the time when they could take their place not under communal or racial labels, but as part and parcel of the whole Indian community.

Now, Sir, with your permission, I want to say a few words with regard to the speeches made against the motion of Sardar Patel. I take first Mr. Muhammad Ismail of Madras. He wants separate electorate. I appeal to his not to ask the charity. Asking for separate electorates is nothing but asking for charity. I tell him that the consequences will be terrible. The majority community will never trust you then. You will never be able to expert yourself. You will be isolated, you will be treated as an alien and your position will be the same as that of the Scheduled Caste. You are not poor. Like the Scheduled Castes, you are not weak, you are not uneducated; you are not uncultured; you can always support yourself. You have produced brilliant men. So do not ask for protection or safeguard. You must have self-confidence in you.  You must expert yourself. You must get into the Assembly by open competition. The times have changed. Adjust yourself. You admitted yesterday in your speech that the atmosphere is better now. I entirely agree with you that the atmosphere is better now. I appeal to you, do not spoil that atmosphere. Improve it, but do not spoil it and if you insist on separate electorate, you will spoil atmosphere very badly. If you get separate electorates, it will again become as bad as before. Say to yourself, Mr. Ismail, that you are an Indian first and an Indian last. Then you will forget all about separate electorates. You will never think of it again.

I will tell you, Sir, that when I had sent in my amendment to clause 292 that it should be deleted, that there should be no reservation of seats, then several Muslim friends to mine, who were for reservation of seats asked me. “Do you realize that the mentality of the Hindus is such at present that if there were no reservation of seats for the Muslims, the Muslims can never succeed?” That honourable gentleman for whom I have got great esteem told me: “Look at us. We have always been with the Congress; we have been to jail and all that. No doubt we will get a ticket from the Congress; many Muslims will get tickets from Socialists and Communists and from other organisations, but what about the electorates? They will never elect you and they will never elect us. So, if there is no reservation, no Muslims will get in because of the mentality of the Hindus.” I told him, Sir, what I am telling you now. I said that I entirely agreed with him that the mentality of the Hindus is such at present. I say to Mr. Ismail also that as long as there is reservation of seats or separate electorate the mentality of the Hindus will never change. You do away with these two things and the mentality will automatically change. I do not want to go into the history of this mentality. I am not going to apportion blame as that will take a long time and you have allotted me a short time and I want to be brief and finish my speech within that time. You all know how the mentality of the Hindus became such, but we have to live in this country, we must change their mentality and it is our duty to change their mentality and the only way the mentality can be changed is to become a part and parcel of the Indian Union. You should say that they are no longer our enemies and then they will be like brothers to us.

Now, Sir, with regard to Mr. Lari, he does not want separate electorates; he does not want reservation of seats; he has condemned both the systems and he says that both the systems are dangerous. He has said that, and I entirely agree with him. He has always opposed separate electorates, reservation of seats and the partition of the country. He is right. But he wants cumulative voting, that is, proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote, or something like that. My honourable Friend, Mr. Saksena has told us that it is a very cumbrous system of mathematical calculations; I am not dealing with that now. The only thing I want to say is that Mr. Lari wants to get into the Assembly by the back door. For example suppose there is a constituency that has to elect four candidates for the House or the People, and there are five candidates. One will be defeated and four will be elected. Out of these five, four are Hindus and one is a Muslim. The votes of the Hindus will be divided among the Hindus and there will get elected. The Muslim will get in on the Muslim votes. Again separate electorates, again reservation of seats. I should like to say to my honourable Friend Mr. Lari if I may say so, that is worse than separate electorate, as the method is not clean. It is not straightforward. I quite understand Mr. Mohamed Ismail’s view when he asks for separate electorates. That is a straightforward method. What is this back-door method of Mr. Lari. I do not understand. I am sure the Muslims do not like these crooked methods; they want a straight, honourable fight. In spite of the fact that Mr. Lari has always openly opposed Pakistan, separate electorates and reservation of seats he still feels inferiority complex. I would ask him to shed this inferiority complex. The country will change for the better.

Last of all, I come to the speech of my honourable and esteemed friend, for whom I have very great regard, Sir Saadulla, the Ex-Premier of Assam. He complains before us that the majority of the Muslim members of the Advisory Committee on Minorities Fundamental Rights etc., did not support the resolution that there should be no reservation of seats for the Muslims. I have already told you, Sir, that I have very great esteem and regard for the Ex-premier of Assam, but I am afraid I must differ from him on this point. I sent my resolution to the Committee to the effect that there should be no reservation of seats. My resolution was discussed under the Chairmanship of the Honourable Sardar Patel. I spoke on my resolution. Begum Aizaz Rasul supported me. Maulana Azad was present there; he did not oppose me. The only person who opposed me was my honourable friend Jafar Imam, from Bihar. There too, I had a majority: Begum Aizaz Rasul. Maulana Azad and myself as against one. The meeting could not be finished and was adjourned sine die. Then it was held on the 11th of this month. I wanted to attend that meeting, particularly because my resolution was there I wanted to move it again. But I never received notice of the meeting. The notice was lying in Delhi; it never reached me. If I had got notice of the meeting. I would have attended it. When I came to Delhi, I learnt that there was the meeting that day. I was happy to learn that the substance of my resolution had been accepted though I was absent. I sent a statement to the Press why I could not attend the meeting that day and it was published in all the papers. Sir Saadulla could not attend the meeting; I do not know why. That meeting was attended by four honourable members: Maulana Azad, Maulana Hifizur Rahman, Begum Aizaz Rasul and Mr. Jaffar Imam. Maulana Azad and Maulana Hifizur Rehman did not oppose my resolution that there should be no reservation of seats.

Every member of this House does not speak. If he oppose, he opposes. If he does not speak, but says “I vote for it“, then he is with it. Maulana Azad was present. If he wanted to oppose, he would have opposed. The two Maulanas did not oppose begum Aizaz Rasul supported my resolution in substance. The resolution was moved by my honourable Friend Dr. Mookherjee. It was the same as my own. Begum Aizaz Rasul supported it. My honourable Friend Mr. Jaffar Imam opposed it. If the Maulana were not with my resolution, they would have sided with Jafar Imam. They said nothing. Votes were taken. There was a clear majority. The Honourable Sardar Patel, I understand, declared that the Muslims were in favour of the motion in spite of the two Maulanas remaining silent. It means that they were with me: three to one voting: there was a majority.

I believe, -I do not remember exactly-there are seven Muslim members on the Committee. Only two are opposed to my resolution; five are with me. The two who are against me are my Hon’ble friends Sir Saadulla and Mr. Jafar Imam. The five who are in favour are , Maulana Azad, Maulana Hifizur Rahman, Begum Aizaz Rasul, Mr. Husseinboy Laljee and myself. Mr. Laljee’s views are well known. He opposed Mr. Jinnah. I know his views. In fact,he wrote to me once, “For God’s sake do something to remove reservations.” Therefore, I had an overwhelming majority. There was another member Syed Ali Zaheer. He is now an Ambassador; I know his views. He is also of the same view as I am.

The next point of my esteemed Friend Sir Saadulla is this. He says, ‘let us take the vote of the Muslim Members here.’ That is a challenge thrown to us. I accept the challenge. I may remind my honourable Friend Sir Saadulla that when the Muslim members came here to Delhi for the first time there was a meeting of all the Muslim members in Western Court. All of them were present. I was the first man to have got up and said that there should be no reservation of seats. I sent my resolution to the Constituent Assembly when you, Sir, were presiding. I regret to say, except one, not a single member supported me. I found that the Muslims wanted reservation. So, I did not move my resolution. text:
Illegal Infiltration & Fake Documentation:-A Real Case I Handled

Home Minister @AmitShah ji has held that the population of Muslims in India has increased due to illegal infiltration. Let me share a real case I personally handled about 5–6 years ago in Mumbai, one among many that reveal how deep this problem runs. Please do read to understand the rot.

1. The Client’s Request:- One evening after court hours, a Muslim gentleman known to me came to my office. He had given his premises in Govandi, Mumbai, on a leave and license agreement to a family of 6/7 people.
Even after the agreement expired, the family refused to vacate.

I perused his papers and assured him of appropriate legal action. He then asked if the matter could be resolved sooner than usual.
When I explained that such cases typically take little time, he hesitated and what he said next stunned me.

2. The Shocking Revelation :- He quietly said, “Sir, those tenants are not Indians, they are Bangladeshis.”

That single sentence changed everything. Two thoughts struck me instantly:
1. Why hadn’t he mentioned this earlier?
2. How did they even get valid Aadhaar and PAN cards as visible in the agreement?

3. The Investigation:- On examining the documents, everything looked perfectly legitimate; Aadhaar, PAN, ration card, even voter ID.
We filed RTIs, involved the local police, and began to dig deeper.

Gradually, the truth surfaced, the birth certificate forming the basis of all these documents was forged.

Using that single forged certificate from 1967, the accused had created a full legal identity for himself and his family, including Aadhaar, PAN, ration card, and voter ID.

4. A Web of Fraud:- It didn’t stop there. The man had used the same method to obtain documents for his wife and children. His son was even married to an Indian Muslim woman, effectively merging into the Indian population.

During the investigation, we uncovered an organized network, a full-fledged industry operating to regularize illegal immigrants by manufacturing fake Indian identities that pass every verification test.

5. The Larger Problem:-India’s diversity makes such infiltration even easier. People entering from Bangladesh, Pakistan, Myanmar, or Nepal often resemble locals making visual identification almost impossible.

Add to this the corruption that exists from border checkpoints to administrative offices, and you have a perfect ecosystem for illegal population growth.

In this very case, we found the involvement of certain officials, and shockingly, even a few lawyers.

6. A Moment That Exposed the Rot:- One of those lawyers, representing the Bangladeshi accused, told my Muslim junior,
“How can you do this? This is a matter of religion.”
My junior stood firm and warned him of a complaint before the Bar Council.

This single moment revealed how some individuals, blinded by religious or political motives, are actively protecting those who illegally enter and settle in India.

7. The Unanswered Question:- 
This wasn’t the only case, I have come across several similar ones.
Despite being aware of this menace for years, successive governments have failed to implement a robust national mechanism to identify and deport such individuals.

8. The Hope:- Now that the Home Minister himself has spoken openly about the issue, one can only hope it translates into real, concrete action. India needs a firm, technology-backed, corruption-proof mechanism to detect and remove non-Indians living here on forged documents.

Illegal infiltration is not just a demographic concern, it’s a threat to national integrity, law, and fairness. The time for acknowledgment is over.
The time for action has arrived.

@AmitShahOffice

text:
I have my twitter back. 

It took me 6 days, a cyber police complaint and a legal notice to twitter to recover my account. 

If you got a DM from me last week asking you to vote for me for a podcast, that was not me. Please don't click it & If you already did, please change your password ASAP.

Here's what happened:

→I received a late night DM from a friend to vote on a podcast which redirected me to a a login page that looked right, and I typed in my password (classic)

→The attacker logged in and changed my 2FA within minutes & I was locked out of my account. (I still don't understand how my email and phone number were changed. Neither my email nor my phone was compromised.)

→Then he used account to DM followers a fake "vote for me" link. Each person who clicks becomes the next account sending it. That is how these spread.

What didn't work:

→ I filed X's hacked account form within the hour. Less than two hours later, the reply came: X could not verify me as the account owner. Their suggestion was to create a new account. Once 2FA is changed, the automated system treats the attacker as the real owner.

→ So I went to the Grievance Officer. Under the IT Rules, 2021, X must appoint a Resident Grievance Officer in India. He has no email address. X does not accept legal notices by email. 

The only options are a web form or post to their physical office.

Here's what worked:

→First, a cyber complaint on https://t.co/Uzds8BObDW (or call 1930).

→Second, a legal notice to the Grievance Officer. Under the IT Rules, impersonation complaints must be acted on within 24 hours.

→Third, the same notice sent by registered post, and to every X email address I could find.

The notice put X on record. It set out the ticket number, the phishing link, and the cyber complaint number. It showed proof of ownership: the registered email, the phone number, and the Premium subscription paid from my card. It ended with a clear ask and a deadline.

Six days after the hack, I was back in.

If this happens to you:
• Act within hours
• File X's hacked account form from your registered email and be persistent (this is important)
• File at https://t.co/Uzds8BObDW and keep the acknowledgement
• Notice to the Grievance Officer via the https://t.co/YkDfcMQwzE form and by post

text:
MeitY's advisory to Meta directs the suppression of protest reporting on Instagram and Facebook. It must be withdrawn.

19 Oct 2026

On 10 October 2026, the Cyber Laws Division of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology issued an advisory to Meta Platforms bearing File No. 6(2)/2026-Cyberlaws. It was not published on the MEITY website and first HT and then PTI reported it on 18 October. Any such advisory is not a legal order and MEITY is not legally empowered to issue them on the basis of any statutory provision. This advisory followed, by two days, an advisory of 8 October to all social media intermediaries calling for "enhanced diligence" over content on "ongoing public events", asking platforms to "label or add context" to misleading content and to "give priority to complaints from authorised Government agencies".  IFF called for the withdrawal of that advisory on 9 October. The Meta advisory was issued on the day the Delhi Police detained protesters and journalists at the demonstrations called over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

The advisory states that content relating to "public-order and law and order situations" is being "prominently displayed and recommended" on Meta's platforms and, "when presented without adequate context or disproportionately amplified", "may contribute to public confusion, apprehension and disturbance of public order and social tranquillity". It singles out "unverified or misleading claims regarding the imposition of emergency, restrictions, police action or other official measures". Further, Meta is advised to review its "recommendation and content ranking mechanisms", to ensure its systems "do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives", and to furnish "information or assistance" to law enforcement, "with immediate effect". PTI reports that the Ministry acted on inputs from "agencies" that Meta's platforms were not promoting all "narratives" equally.

This advisory matches restrictions on META platforms related to protest content and reporting in the same timline. On 10 October, the Instagram account of Molitics India was withheld in India. On 11 October, a Mathrubhumi English reel showing a woman clinging to a pole as police officers attempted to detain her was restricted citing, "a notice from the Government of India/Law Enforcement", and a video report by Observer Post Hindi was restricted on Facebook by what Meta called an "automated system" acting under the IT Rules, 2021. On 12 October, the Instagram account of journalist Shubhangi Das Gupta was restricted in India for alleged non-compliance with "local IT Rules". On 13 October, the account of Journo Mirror (about five lakh followers) was withheld. The account of Fridays For Future India has since been withheld without any stated reason. Meta's notices to these users do not disclose what is unlawful about the content. 

As per notices shared by us by those who have been censored by META, they take two forms: 

1. "a notice from the Government of India/Law Enforcement under Section 79(3)(b)", and, 

2. "through an automated system implemented pursuant to legal requirements under India's Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules". 

Neither names the issuing agency, the order, the provision of law or offence the content is said to disclose, or the URL complained of. We know due to litigation that the first notice related to a Sahyog order issued by a Law Enforcement Agency (LEA), while the second one is without any legal order. At the same time, several users received no communication at all. Instagram used the same "automated system" notice against Anjali Priya, Varnika Dhawan and Sachin Gupta after the July protests, and against cartoonist Satish Acharya, who lost nine cartoons and then his account between February and September 2026. 

In April 2026, The Hindu reported that Meta automatically restricts government and police flagged content in India at scale, and seeks a separate government direction before restoring content later found to be legally unsupported. IFF objected to Meta on 4 May 2026. IFF condemns the advisory of 10 October and the restrictions imposed in its wake. An executive communication that instructs a platform to suppress "unverified" claims about "police action" and to correct a "limited set of narratives", issued on the day of a police crackdown and kept from the public, is a censorship directive in all but name.  It makes the State the editor of what Indians may see of a protest against the State. IFF calls upon MeitY to withdraw it and upon Meta to disclose what it has done under it.

Our demands

1. MeitY must withdraw the advisories of 8 and 10 October 2026 forthwith and publish them.

2. MeitY must abandon proposed Rule 3(4) and restrict content only by reasoned, published orders under Section 69A or notices compliant with Rule 3(1)(d).

3. Meta must disclose every takedown, account restriction and act of downranking carried out under the advisories, and its compliance report to the Ministry.

4. Meta must restore the accounts and posts of journalists, outlets and creators restricted since 8 October 2026 unless it holds a valid legal order, and must furnish that order to the person affected.

5. Meta must suspend the automated restriction of content in India and disclose on what inputs its "automated system" acts.

Any person whose account or content has been withheld in India since 8 October 2026 may write to IFF at legal@internetfreedom.in. IFF is providing assistance pro bono.

text:
Statement : The removal of BitChat from the India App Store is unconstitutional. Section 69A permits the blocking of unlawful information, not of a messenger for working during internet shutdowns.

New Delhi, 3 October 2026

An Apple App Review notice published today by Jack Dorsey on X records that BitChat has been removed from the India App Store "per demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology", issued under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act, 2000, on the ground that the application "includes content that is illegal in India". The notice adds that BitChat's TestFlight builds are no longer available for testing in India. It does not identify the content said to be illegal or the ground under Section 69A invoked. The blocking order has not been published. The Internet Freedom Foundation condemns the order and calls for its immediate publication and withdrawal.

BitChat relays end-to-end encrypted messages between nearby phones over Bluetooth mesh. It has no servers and hosts no content of its own. What travels through it is the private speech of its users, so the claim that the application "includes" illegal content is incoherent. The State's actual objection stands recorded in the notices the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre issued on 23 July 2026 to GitHub, Google and Apple against BitChat, Briar and Bridgefy which stated that such applications work even during internet shutdowns and hamper lawful interception, attribution and traceability. Those notices, issued under Section 79(3)(b) were reportedly withdrawn after public disclosure. The same end has now been pursued through Section 69A. The objection is to capability of an application, not to content it transmits. A citizen's ability to speak to another citizen while the State has switched the internet off is not a ground of restriction under Section 69A or Article 19(2) of the Constitution.

Section 69A survived constitutional scrutiny in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) because of its safeguards which included the need for a reasoned, recorded order, committee review, and a hearing to the originator under Rule 8 of the Blocking Rules, 2009, which the Delhi High Court enforced in Tanul Thakur v. Union of India (2022). Further, Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020) requires that orders restricting fundamental rights be published and adopt the least restrictive measure. However, it appears in this instance, each safeguard has been evaded. A secret order blocking an entire application, rather than any identified unlawful information, is the most restrictive and disproprotionate measure available. Further, the confidentiality claimed under Rule 16 cannot defeat the right to challenge an order, and the constitutionality of this blocking regime is itself pending consideration before the Supreme Court.

While removal from the App Store does not delete BitChat from phones, it stops new downloads and security updates, leaving existing users on unpatched versions, and it ends security testing in India through TestFlight. During the Jantar Mantar protests, when mobile internet was suspended and jammers were deployed, Bluetooth mesh messaging was a channel of last resort through which young people coordinated their safety. To our knowledge, Apple has removed BitChat on a government's demand in only one other country. This is in China, in April this year.

Our demands

1. MeitY must publish the blocking order, the ground invoked and the record of the committee's proceedings, and serve the developers with a copy and an opportunity of hearing.

2. The direction must be withdrawn. Any specific unlawful use must be met with targeted proceedings under due process, not the removal of a communications tool for everyone.

3. Apple must disclose the demand in its transparency reporting and notify its users in India, and must state whether parallel directions have been received in respect of other app stores.

4. The secrecy of the blocking regime must end. The Blocking Rules, 2009 should be amended to require publication of orders and notice to originators, without awaiting the outcome of the pending constitutional challenge.

The Internet Freedom Foundation will file applications under the Right to Information Act seeking a copy of the order, and stands ready to assist the developers and affected users in India.

text:
Take $1 million a head, remove qualified immunity permanently !

If you enter or remain on someone else's property without their approval and refuse to leave after being explicitly told to do so, you can be charged with criminal trespass. 

*Having the encounter recorded on video provides direct evidence of the homeowner's explicit demands and your refusal to comply, which strongly supports criminal prosecution.

Charges and Legal Consequences

• Criminal Trespass: 
In almost all jurisdictions, remaining on a property after receiving an explicit notice or demand to leave by the owner turns the situation into a clear act of criminal trespass. This is typically classified as a misdemeanor, punishable by fines, probation, or jail time.

• Burglary or Breaking and Entering: 
If you entered an occupied structure (like a house) without permission with the intent to commit a crime inside (even a minor crime), you could face felony burglary charges.

• Disturbing the Peace / Disorderly Conduct: 
If the refusal to leave involves shouting, aggressive behavior, or creating a public disturbance, law enforcement may add these charges.

• Civil Liability: 
Beyond criminal charges, the homeowner can sue you in civil court for damages under tort law for trespassing on their private property.

The Role of the Constitution

**The United States Constitution primarily restricts government actions, not private citizens. However, it applies to this situation in the following ways:

• Property Rights and Privacy: 
While the Constitution protects individuals from government overreach (such as the Fourth Amendment protecting against unreasonable searches by police), it implicitly recognizes and upholds private property laws established by states. A private homeowner has the right to control who enters their home.

• No First Amendment Protection for Trespassing: You cannot claim a constitutional right to "free speech" or "protest" to remain on private property against the owner's will. The First Amendment does not protect individuals who violate criminal laws on private residential property.

• Due Process: 
If you are arrested, your Constitutional rights (such as the Fifth and Sixth Amendments) guarantee you the right to a fair trial, due process, and legal representation. The video evidence will be used during this process.

Important Legal Distinctions

*The speed at which law enforcement can act depends heavily on your relationship to the property:
• Uninvited Guests/Intruders: 
If you have no connection to the home, police can generally remove you immediately for criminal trespass.

• Established Tenants or Squatters: 
If you have lived there, paid rent, received mail, or were previously granted long-term access, a court may view you as having established residency. In that case, even if the homeowner demands you leave on video, they cannot forcibly remove you or change the locks immediately; they must go through a formal, legal eviction process

Where the Central Government or any of its officer specially authorized by it in this behalf is satisfied that it is necessary or expedient so to do, in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India, defense of India, security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States or public order or for preventing incitement to the commission of any cognizable offence relating to above, it may subject to the provisions of sub-section (2) for reasons to be recorded in writing, by order, direct any agency of the Government or intermediary to block for access by the public or cause to be blocked for access by the public any information generated, transmitted, received, stored or hosted in any computer resource.

2. The procedure and safeguards subject to which such blocking for access by the public may be carried out, shall be such as may be prescribed.

3. The intermediary who fails to comply with the direction issued under sub-section (1) shall be punished with an imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine.

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

This issue may look small, but similar issues are happening everywhere, and no one is noticing them.  In March 2026, ahead of the Kerala Assembly elections (polling on 9 April 2026), a 2019 Election Commission of India (ECI) letter redistributed by the Kerala Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office was found to carry the seal of the BJP’s Kerala unit. This sparked a political row, followed by police-directed efforts to remove related social media posts

This takedown action itself became controversial, with critics framing it as an attempt to suppress discussion of an official lapse during an election period, while authorities maintained it was necessary to stop the circulation of a withdrawn and erroneous document that was being used to question the ECI’s credibility.The episode remained a flashpoint in the final stretch of the Kerala campaign, with the ECI treating it as a corrected administrative mistake and the opposition presenting it as evidence of deeper concerns about the poll body’s independence.The letter and the seal
The document was an ECI communication dated 19 March 2019 containing guidelines/FAQs on the publicity of candidates’ criminal antecedents (following a Supreme Court judgment). CPI(M) and Congress shared versions online showing the BJP Kerala unit’s seal. It had been circulated by the Kerala CEO’s office to political parties, District Election Officers, and Returning Officers as part of clarifications around mid-March 2026.thesouthfirst.comKerala CEO / ECI explanation:
It was described as a “purely clerical error.” The BJP Kerala unit had approached the CEO’s office seeking clarification on the (by then revised) 2019 guidelines and submitted a photocopy of the original directive that already bore the party’s seal. Staff overlooked this and redistributed that version. The error was identified; on 21 March a formal withdrawal notice was issued telling recipients to disregard the document. An Assistant Section Officer was suspended pending inquiry. Later, a Deputy CEO and a Section Officer were relieved of election-related duties.livemint.comOpposition parties (CPI(M) and Congress) rejected the clerical-error account. They alleged compromised institutional neutrality, claiming seals were being “casually swapped” and questioning whether the ECI and BJP shared the same “power centre.” Some BJP responses labelled the circulation of the old document as misinformation or a political plot.thewire.inDeletion of posts controversyActing on an ECI directive (under the Model Code of Conduct), the Kerala Police cyber cell issued notices to X (Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, and numerous individual accounts. They demanded removal of posts sharing the letter that carried the BJP seal.  Police argued the content insulted the Election Commission, undermined its integrity and transparency, spread false claims about a rectified clerical error, and risked public order or communal harmony by potentially fuelling political division.
